extracted.intended_audience: national and local public health authorities, emergency communication practitioners, and journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, building and implementing risk communication during public health emergencies, including policy, training, media engagement, simulation exercises and operational deployment support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk communication as an essential lifesaving action
rubrics_metrics.description: In public health emergencies, one essential lifesaving action is risk communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People have a right to know how to protect their health and have a responsibility to take informed decisions to protect themselves, their loved ones and those around them. Effective risk communication not only saves lives and reduces illness, it enables countries and communities to preserve their social, economic and political stability in the face of emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize rights and responsibilities in communication
rubrics_metrics.description: People have a right to know how to protect their health and have a responsibility to take informed decisions to protect themselves, their loved ones and those around them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames objectives for communication: ensure the public has timely, actionable information and encourage individual/collective actions to reduce harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include risk communication as an IHR core capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication is one of 8 core capacities in order to prevent the global spread of disease as required under the International Health Regulations (2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk communication should be integrated into national IHR implementation plans and monitored as a core preparedness capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate risk communication into pandemic preparedness frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk communication is also a component of global and country preparedness for an influenza pandemic, as part of the Pandemic Influenza Preparedness Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure risk-communication activities and plans are incorporated into pandemic planning, including coordination with relevant frameworks and partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish policies, strategies and plans for risk communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing policies, strategies and plans for risk communication;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries should develop formal policies and strategic plans that define objectives, roles, channels, target audiences, and coordination mechanisms for risk communication across all levels of government and partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide training for key personnel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build capacity by training staff and officials responsible for designing and delivering risk communication so they can convey clear, consistent, evidence-based messages under emergency conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage and train journalists on emergency reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging and training journalists on how to report on health emergencies;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work proactively with media professionals to improve accuracy, reduce sensationalism, and ensure responsible reporting that supports public understanding and protective behaviours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run simulation exercises to test national systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Running simulation exercises to test national systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct drills and simulation exercises to evaluate the effectiveness of communication plans, interagency coordination, message delivery, and community reach; use lessons learned to update plans and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide hands-on operational support via Emergency Communications Network
rubrics_metrics.description: WHO provides hands on support in emergency response by deploying its Emergency Communications Network to affected countries and regions to work hand-in-hand with national and local authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational deployment and technical support should be available during emergencies to augment national capacities, coordinate messaging, and assist in rapid information dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use WHO global guidance and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: WHO provides global guidance to countries on the best practices for risk communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Countries and practitioners should draw on WHO’s guidance when designing risk communication activities, policies and training to align with international best practices.
